---
title: "Save Point"
---

::: {.ao-story}
The first seal in the Crypt is a mark on the floor that you can step back to. Soon you will send a companion ahead into the dark, and stone will shift as it rewrites half your corridor in a few heartbeats. The warden says every traveller who walks on without a mark has walked back along that corridor with nothing to show. Make your mark before you touch anything.
:::

::: {.quest-dialog}
- **Goal:** you will make any change reversible before an agent touches it.
- **Before you start:** [Choose What to Hand Over](../basecamp/wade-in.html), a terminal and `git` (the version control tool). A **commit** is a saved snapshot of your project; a **tracked** file is one git already follows.
- **Time:** about 10 minutes.
:::

An agent can edit many files in seconds, and you may want them back as they were. Before any agent edits your files, put them under version control (a record of every saved state of a project):

1. Run `git init` once in the project folder.
2. List large data files in a `.gitignore` file first (for example a line `*.fastq.gz`), or git stores a copy of each. Then run `git add -A && git commit -m "before agent"`.
3. Let the agent work. If it breaks something, run `git restore --staged --worktree .` to return every **tracked** file to that commit. (Plain `git restore .` copies from the staging area, so it keeps anything you or the agent staged with `git add`.)

`git restore --staged --worktree .` has two limits:

- It also throws away **your own** uncommitted edits to tracked files, so commit before you start.
- It leaves **new, untracked** files the agent created where they are. `git status` shows them, and you delete them yourself.

## Lore

*Further reading. Optional.*

- [Checkpointing](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/checkpointing): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it explains `/rewind` and its limits, including that Bash-made changes need version control, so you see why git is the real save point.
- [Manage sessions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it lists the commands for naming, resuming and clearing sessions, including `claude --resume`, a companion when work is interrupted.
:::
